notes.title: 🕹️ Console Factory — Your Creativity in LCD Style
notes.content:
[h2]🕹️ Console Factory — Your Creativity in LCD Style[/h2][p]The LCD mini game era is back, and now [b]you’re the designer[/b].
The new [b]Console Factory[/b] feature, available right at launch on [i]Mini Games Retro 90s[/i] for Steam, allows players to [b]create their own retro handheld consoles[/b], inspired by the beloved classics of the 80s and 90s.[/p][p]Get ready for a true time-traveling experience — with total creative freedom![/p][previewyoutube="Gp7bI5DsYwI;full"][/previewyoutube][hr][/hr][h3]🎮 How does it work?[/h3][p]Start with one of the 20+ classic mini games already included in the collection, and turn that base into something completely unique:[/p][p]🔧 [b]Choose a base game:[/b]
Begin with any of the existing games like [i]Car Racing[/i], [i]Tennis[/i], or [i]Soccer[/i].[/p][p]🎨 [b]Customize your console:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Pick from different console shell models[/p][/*][*][p]Choose your own shell colors[/p][/*][*][p]Paint each button to your liking[/p][/*][*][p]Name your custom game[/p][/*][/list][p]🖼️ [b]Edit the game graphics:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Replace each LCD sprite individually[/p][/*][*][p]Use your own artwork or draw in classic monochrome style[/p][/*][*][p]Modify background and interface elements of the console[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686150/1d28e87ddbf55bb1c49f6f490607ad9c2f292408.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3]📦 Save and Play[/h3][p]Create as many consoles as you want! Best of all: everything is saved in-game and always accessible whenever you want to play.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🧒 A Tribute and a Reinvention[/h2][p]In the 90s, mini games came pre-made — the idea of crafting your own handheld console was unthinkable. Now, it’s not only possible — it’s faithful to the [b]original aesthetic[/b]:[/p][p]🔲 Authentic black-and-white LCD style
📢 Classic beeping sounds
📉 Pre-drawn frame-by-frame animation
🕹️ Simple, addictive, nostalgic gameplay[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🚀 When?[/h3][p][b]Console Factory[/b] will be available at the game’s official launch on Steam,
[b]September 16, 2025[/b].[/p][p]No DLC, no future update — it’s part of the game [b]on day one[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🔥 Get Ready to Build the Mini Game of Your Dreams[/h3][p]Remember spending hours with just one LCD game in your hands?
Now imagine having [b]your own name[/b] on the shell.
Or seeing [b]your own character[/b] on the black-and-white screen.[/p][p]That’s the essence of Console Factory: [b]blending nostalgia with creativity[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3844720/Mini_Games_Retro_90s"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: The History of LCD Mini Games: From 90s Craze to PC Revival
notes.content: [h3]🕹️ The History of LCD Mini Games: A Journey Through Digital Nostalgia[/h3][p]Before smartphones filled our pockets — and long before modern handheld consoles — a craze took over millions of childhoods: the [b]LCD mini games[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686150/86e8f41002aa00cab2c76b012caa17d245d1c274.png"][/img][/p][p]These tiny electronic devices, with simple graphics and minimal buttons, taught a generation how to have fun with just the essentials. Each unit had only one game (and lots of imagination), delivering thrilling challenges and hours of fun — no internet, no saves, no updates needed.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🎮 Origins: From Gunpei Yokoi to the World[/h3][p]It all started with Nintendo, when Gunpei Yokoi created the iconic [b]Game & Watch[/b] series in the late 1970s. These handhelds featured monochrome LCD screens and basic, yet brilliant, controls. They were groundbreaking for electronic entertainment.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686150/7bc35fa039cfeaca3e2a3e09ea03dabdb508e2c3.png"][/img][/p][p]Photo by [url="https://unsplash.com/pt-br/@tonizaat?utm_content=creditCopyText&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=unsplash"]Toni Zaat[/url] on [url="https://unsplash.com/pt-br/fotografias/brinquedo-robo-branco-e-vermelho-FownOKydHCI?utm_content=creditCopyText&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=unsplash"]Unsplash[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Inspired by their success, companies around the world launched their own versions of LCD mini games, especially across Asia. Soon, these devices flooded street markets, newspaper stands, and toy stores. They had colorful looks, beeping soundtracks, and a wide range of themes: [b]racing[/b], [b]soccer[/b], [b]ninjas[/b], [b]submarines[/b], [b]basketball[/b], [b]tennis[/b], and more.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🐯 Tiger Electronics and the “Single Licensed Game” Craze[/h3][p]In the U.S. and other countries, Tiger Electronics dominated the LCD mini game market throughout the 90s. The company became famous for licensing popular franchises like [b]Power Rangers[/b], [b]Street Fighter[/b], [b]Sonic[/b], [b]Batman[/b], [b]Jurassic Park[/b], [b]X-Men[/b], and many more.[/p][p]These handhelds followed the traditional mini game format, with static LCD screens and limited controls — typically just [b]left[/b], [b]right[/b], [b]up[/b], [b]down[/b], [b]attack[/b], and [b]jump[/b] buttons. Each device featured only one game, but the visual appeal was key: the casing and background artwork were filled with vibrant illustrations of characters and settings.[/p][p]Despite their simplicity and repetitive gameplay, Tiger games sold millions of units and remain collectible to this day. For many kids outside Japan, these were their first experience with character-themed handheld gaming.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🧸 In Brazil: Tectoy and the Local Craze[/h3][p]In Brazil, [b]Tectoy[/b] was responsible for importing — and even producing — local versions of many electronic toys, including licensed LCD mini games. The company partnered with iconic local brands like [b]Monica’s Gang[/b], [b]Yellow Woodpecker Ranch[/b], and even [b]The Powerpuff Girls[/b].[/p][p]These mini games were bestsellers at newsstands and toy shops. Despite being technically simple, their appeal came from their characters and portability. Many of them had only one or two action buttons, yet still managed to keep players hooked with increasing difficulty.[/p][p]For many Brazilians, these games were the gateway to the world of handheld gaming — and are fondly remembered to this day.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🌎 “Paraguayan Mini Games” — The Street Kings of Brazilian Childhood[/h3][p]For those who grew up in Brazil in the 80s and 90s, the so-called “[b]Paraguayan mini games[/b]” were a cultural phenomenon. Despite the nickname, many of these consoles didn't actually come from Paraguay — but rather from China, Korea, or Taiwan, arriving through alternative trade routes and being widely sold in street markets, fairs, newsstands, and of course… during trips to Ciudad del Este.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686150/aa0d919a5a558eb9f3fc6575112d908458272386.png"][/img][/p][p]Beyond the gameplay, they stood out for their design. The colorful plastic shells, the bold action stickers, and the printed backgrounds on the LCD made them feel like holding a futuristic piece of retro digital art. Simple as they were, these devices had a kind of magic:[/p][list][*][p][b]Addictive beeping sound effects[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Monochrome LCD graphics[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Colorful plastic casings with generic artwork[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Each round felt like a battle against time — and your own reflexes. These “Paraguayan” handhelds were accessible, portable, and above all, [b]fun[/b]. All you needed was a tiny LR44 battery and boom — hours of gameplay in school, on the bus, or at home.[/p][p]Flaws aside — loud volume with no control, screens that faded over time, limited variety — these mini games defined a whole generation of Brazilian gamers and are remembered with great affection.[/p][p]And who could forget the legendary [b]“9999 in 1”[/b]? Despite the exaggerated number, most of these games reused the same gameplay with speed variations or mirrored challenges. Still… totally irresistible![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686150/e6c74d2cc10f09826f345f645235160e77241dee.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3]🔁 The Legacy Lives On[/h3][p]Today, LCD mini games are cherished collector’s items, remembered fondly by nostalgic fans around the world. They represent an era of creativity, simplicity, and unforgettable fun.[/p][p]With [b]Mini Games Retro 90s[/b], our mission is to bring that world back — in full authenticity. This project is a direct tribute to those devices: from the UI to the sound effects, from the visuals to the gameplay. It’s more than nostalgia — it’s a respectful recreation of one of gaming culture’s most iconic chapters.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Here are a few real screenshots from games featured in Mini Games Retro 90s:[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686150/19400a463cbf3ec1f79e5e3fb70e2d090fcdeb53.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]📅 [b]Don’t forget to add the game to your Wishlist here on Steam![/b][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3844720"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]📱 Want to play it now? The app is already available for Android and iOS:[/p][list][*][p][url="https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.wantrobapps.minigames"]📲 Google Play[/url][/p][/*][*][p][url="https://apps.apple.com/app/mini-games-retro-90s/id6677063007"]🍎 App Store[/url][/p][/*][/list][p]💬 Tell us in the comments: which mini game marked your childhood?[/p]
